searchText: > <@!135612611923279872> Are those for 1559? <@!301186049323958275> The top ones are 1559, the bottom ones are escalator. The bottom ones *could* work as a hybrid design too, but there were also some ideas shared verbally on the call that we should sketch up for other ways to achieve an even better hybrid design. Why is the range so high for the top left mockup? The most the base_fee can change in a block is 1/8, which means during a time of transient congestion it will double every 2 minutes. If your target is 4 minutes, you would have $0.2 - $0.6 (using the $0.2 from your example as current), 6 minutes would be $0.2 - $0.8. Personally, I would probably build tools targeting 2 minute inclusion in all but the worst case scenarios, so $0.2 - $0.4. If the numbers were "random numbers and shouldn't be taken seriously" then feel free to ignore. 🙂 I'm just worried because there is a lot of confusion around expected behavior post-1559, and I want to make sure people don't actually think that a range like $0.2 to $1 is reasonable (given current parameter choices). Hi all, here's the transcript from the call: https://notes.ethereum.org/@afhGjrKfTKmksTOtqhB9RQ/BkDkCBAoI Bleh, after I sit through most of the call. 😛 <@!552133098075193354> i think it does make sense to release the video call publicly (youtube), these are important protocal decisions and i think in a few years it will be very insightful to look back. unless there is opposition by participants <@!439193900096290816> ^ maybe worth skimming for the related network monitoring experiment
